root.name: Sicilian Defense: Paulsen-Basman Defense
root.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 e6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Bc5

overview: Black develops the bishop to c5 early, hitting the d4 knight, and White usually plays Nb3, Bb6 or Be3, gaining time against the bishop. Black gets a slightly passive but solid ...e6 Sicilian set-up with quick castling, while White has space and extra development. I am unsure of the details of this line.

white_ideas.idea: Chase the bishop with Nb3, then develop Nc3, Bf4 or Bg5 and castle.
Use the lead in development and the space edge.

black_ideas.idea: Use the half-open c-file and aim for ...d5 or ...Qb6 counterplay.

typical_structures.structure: Sicilian asymmetry with White's e4 and d4 pieces, Black's ...e6 chain and half-open c-file.

character.notes: Black is slightly passive but solid; White's lead in development gives chances.

structure.notes: Sicilian pawn asymmetry with a half-open c-file.

approach.notes: Rarely chosen by strong players; a surprise-oriented move order.

character.reason: Early bishop development but not especially solid or sharp.

soundness.reason: Playable, if slightly worse for Black.
